note: Revision Log Default is a zero-config behaviour module: one hook_entity_presave() that fills an empty revision log message on any ContentEntity implementing RevisionLogInterface. New entity => 'Created new <bundle label>' (e.g. 'Created new Article'); new translation => 'Created <language> translation'; update => 'Updated the <Field label> field' (list of changed field labels) or 'Updated <bundle label>'. It never overwrites a provided message. No configure route, no permissions, no Drush, no plugins, no config schema. Medium cases are grounded in real generated state: setup saves a node so the module fills the message, agent reads it back via drush. Hard cases require the agent to create/edit a node WITHOUT a log message and let the module populate it, verified against the live node's revision log message.

evals.prompt: I enabled the Revision Log Default module. When I save a brand-new Article node without typing a revision log message, what message does it record, and which hook produces it?
evals.expected_output: For a new entity it records 'Created new <bundle label>', e.g. 'Created new Article'. It is produced by revision_log_default_entity_presave() (hook_entity_presave), which only fills the message when it is empty.

evals.prompt: Does the Revision Log Default module overwrite a revision log message I typed myself? Which entities does it act on, and when does it decide to generate a message?
evals.expected_output: It never overwrites a message you provided; it only acts when getRevisionLogMessage() is empty. It runs on save (hook_entity_presave) for content entities that implement RevisionLogInterface (nodes and other revisionable types).

evals.prompt: With Revision Log Default enabled, if I edit a node and change one field (say the Title) and save a new revision without a log message, what revision log message gets generated? And how does the module handle content-moderation workflows?
evals.expected_output: It diffs the entity against its original and records 'Updated the <Field label> field' (e.g. 'Updated the Title field'), listing multiple changed field labels if several changed, or 'Updated <label>' if none can be identified. For content_moderation/workbench_moderation entities it diffs against the latest revision rather than the default revision.

evals.prompt: On this site an Article node titled 'RLD Known Created' was just created without anyone typing a revision log message. Inspect the live node and report the revision log message that was recorded for it.
evals.expected_output: Its revision log message is 'Created new Article', auto-generated by revision_log_default because the node was saved with an empty message.

evals.prompt: On this site the Article node titled 'RLD Known Update EDITED' had its title changed and a new revision saved with no revision log message. Inspect the node's latest revision and report the revision log message that Revision Log Default generated.
evals.expected_output: The latest revision log message reports the changed field(s), starting with 'Updated the Title field' (it may also list other changed fields), generated automatically because the message was left empty.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, create and save an Article node with the title 'RLD Hard Created' and do NOT set any revision log message. Let the Revision Log Default module supply the message. Apply this to the live site.
evals.expected_output: After creating the Article 'RLD Hard Created' without a revision log message, the node's revision log message is auto-populated with 'Created new Article' by revision_log_default_entity_presave().

evals.prompt: On this site there is an Article node titled 'RLD Hard Update'. Edit it: change its title to 'RLD Hard Update EDITED' and save it as a new revision, without writing any revision log message. Let Revision Log Default generate the message. Apply this to the live site.
evals.expected_output: The node is retitled 'RLD Hard Update EDITED' with a new revision (>=2 revisions), and its latest revision log message was auto-generated to report the changed field, e.g. 'Updated the Title field'.
